SOURCE EXCERPT:
A student on academic probation is limited to twelve credit hours in the following semester and must meet an adviser before registration opens. Probation is triggered by a semester grade point average below 2.0 or by a cumulative average below 2.0; a student who triggers it on the semester average alone while holding a cumulative average of 2.5 or higher is placed on notice instead, which carries the adviser meeting but no credit limit. Probation is cleared when the cumulative average reaches 2.0 at the end of a semester in which the student completed at least nine credit hours. A second consecutive semester on probation results in academic suspension for one calendar year, and a suspended student may petition for early reinstatement only after two full semesters have passed. Grades earned elsewhere during a suspension do not transfer. Courses dropped after the published withdrawal deadline count as attempted hours for the completion requirement.
